problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [-2,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,-1]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-0.917$ |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 3{y}^{4} & 3{y}^{2}+12x{y}^{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 3{y}^{4} & 3{y}^{2}+12x{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 3{y}^{4} & 3{y}^{2}+12x{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 3(-1)^{4} & 3(-1)^{2}+12(-1)(-1)^{3}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1)(-1)-1 \\ (-1)^{3}+3(-1)(-1)^{4}+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 3 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot 15-(-1)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}15 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{12} \\ -\frac{11}{12}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.083 \\ -0.917\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
